sources.document_title: Questionnaire on the Electronic Money Directive (2000/46/EC)
sources.document_version: Ref. E-Money003/2005; public consultation document of Commission services (DG Internal Market)
sources.pinpoint: PDF/printed p6, item11 and questions11(a)–(b); cover p1.
sources.brief_exact_phrase: prevent the lighter regulated ELMIs from competing with banks for deposits
sources.page_context_paraphrase: Item11 is a retrospective statement by Commission services about negotiations preceding EMD1. It attributes the proposal to unnamed Member States and then asks whether a prohibition is needed. It does not identify the proposing states or furnish their original papers. The surrounding page moves from waivers to interest and then scope; this is holder interest on funds exchanged for e-money, not issuer reserve earnings.
sources.verification_result: Claim supported with the manuscript’s existing attribution and limits. Treat this as official retrospective evidence, not proof of a named national submission.

sources.document_title: Council ST 5575/09, Presidency compromise on EMD2
sources.document_version: Council ST5575/09 INIT;21January2009; Presidency compromise following14January working-party meeting
sources.pinpoint: PDF/printed p22, Article10c; cover p1 states version/comparison conventions.
sources.brief_exact_phrase: [unless these funds constitute deposits or other repayable funds
sources.page_context_paraphrase: Article10c bans interest or other benefits tied to the duration of holding e-money, then contains an express square-bracketed exception. The exception refers cumulatively to deposits or repayable funds under Directive2006/48/EC Article4(1) and deposits under Directive94/19/EC Article1(1). The closing bracket is immediately before the final full stop. The full clause is bold and underlined in this version. Page1 explains underlining as changes against the Commission proposal, (…) as deletions, and bold as changes against the last compromise. These are drafting conventions, not proof that this was the earliest-ever formulation.
sources.verification_result: Claim supported. Preserve bracketed status and avoid an unqualified claim that January2009 was the rule’s first drafting origin.

sources.document_title: CP117 The regulation of electronic money issuers
sources.document_version: FSA ConsultationPaper117, December2001;200-page archived original including annexes
sources.pinpoint: PDF pp43–44/printed pp42–43, paras6.35–6.37 and Q12; cover p1 and contents/copyright p2.
sources.page_context_paraphrase: Paragraph6.35 distinguishes interest-rate exposure of backing investments from mismatch between returns received on assets and interest paid on outstanding e-money. It pairs a maturity/reset restriction for assets with a holder-interest ban to contain risk without burdensome measurement/management. Paragraph6.37 expressly calls interest a feature of deposits rather than payment mechanisms, invokes the cash-substitute character of e-money, and acknowledges EMD1 did not then prohibit interest. It is not a ban on the issuer earning reserve interest.
sources.verification_result: Manuscript account supported. Paragraph6.36’s phrasing about losses from declining market rates is a statement in the source, not an economic proposition the manuscript should independently endorse; the manuscript does not rely on that detail.
sources.review_scope: Relevant complete primary pages with adjacent context and cover/version identification; visual verification of decisive pages. Not full-document semantic review. Cover verifies December 2001 only; register day 19 December is retained separately and not treated as a verified printed date.

sources.document_title: The regulation of electronic money issuers: Feedback on CP117
sources.document_version: FSA PolicyStatement, The Regulation of Electronic Money Issuers: Feedback on CP117, April2002;49pages
sources.pinpoint: PDF pp21–22/printed pp20–21, Q12 and Our reply; PDFp46/printedp45 separately discusses discounted issuance; cover p1 and copyright p2.
sources.brief_exact_phrase: not meant to stop promotional activities
sources.page_context_paraphrase: The Q12 summary reports mixed opinions: one criticism of excessive restriction, broad agreement from others qualified by concern about loyalty/cash promotions and asset maturity limits. FSA says it will not amend the rule but explains that free first-load e-money, bonus and loyalty payments are not stopped. Its second reply retains asset restrictions because eliminating liability mismatch does not eliminate market-value risk in interest-bearing backing assets. The account is aggregated: the respondent list does not identify which actor took each position. Printedp45 concerns a separate discounted-issuance clarification requiring a third party to make up the face-value shortfall; it should not be used as the main support for the interest-ban clarification.
sources.verification_result: Current manuscript’s wording “promotional benefits” is correct and supported; no wording repair needed. An earlier visual message suggesting “proportional” was my reading error. Footnote25’s pp20–21 are the decisive support.
sources.review_scope: Relevant complete primary pages with adjacent context and cover/version identification; visual verification of decisive pages. Not full-document semantic review.
sources.rights_note: FSA2002 copyright expressly shown on PDFp2. No general public-redistribution licence established. Same private-original/public-link treatment as CP117; do not assume OGL merely because this is regulatory material.

sources.document_title: UK Finance and Asset and Liability Management Association — consultation response
sources.document_version: Cover page 1: Date: 07 September 2021. Archived respondent-hosted v1.0 PDF, Wayback capture 20210915220157; original bytes retained.
sources.pinpoint: pp 17–19, Q6; pp 23–24, Q10; contextual checks pp 9–11 and 25
sources.brief_exact_phrase: it might restrict or impede the implementation of monetary policy
sources.page_context_paraphrase: Q6 examines both remunerated and unremunerated CBDC/stablecoin scenarios. Non-remuneration can stabilize bank deposits yet impede transmission; changes in policy rates may move funds in the opposite direction to the intended credit effect. Q10 warns that a banking model may obstruct entry and protect incumbents, while declining to choose a final regulatory framework.
sources.verification_result: Supports the manuscript’s analytical counterexample, not an attribution of categorical support for holder remuneration. The generic interest pass-through in Q5 does not identify reserve income. Do not attribute the Bank’s anonymous 2022 income-sharing proposal to these organisations. The Q1 token-lending illustration concerns a separate risk-bearing arrangement.
sources.review_scope: Cover, Q1–2 pp 9–11, Q5–6 pp 17–19 and Q10–11 pp 23–25 rechecked; full-text remuneration search. Prior frozen review records all 25 pages. This verification is targeted, not a second complete recoding.

sources.document_version: Undated contribution; date remains unknown. Cover §1.3 identifies the Bank consultation and refers to FCA consultations published 16 December 2025 and 23 January 2026. sources.brief_exact_phrase: issuers should have the flexibility to determine themselves whether interest on backing assets can and should be passed on
sources.page_context_paraphrase: Section 10 expressly recommends issuer discretion to share backing income, contests the payments/investment boundary, and treats competition for deposits as beneficial. It separately seeks permission and clarity for issuer and non-issuer rewards, including activity rewards. Section 3.2 seeks issuer earnings on backing assets and central-bank deposits subject to liquidity safeguards.
sources.verification_result: Supports A/B permission and separate C/D rewards permission; issuer earnings are E and must not substitute for evidence of holder income. The claim that statutory-trust backing prevents downside is the respondent’s argument, not an independently established legal or prudential fact. The manuscript correctly attributes it. Keep the contribution undated and identify the consultation year separately.

sources.document_title: American Bankers Association and state bankers associations (joint submission) — consultation response
sources.document_version: Letter cover dated May 1, 2026. Register separately records receipt April 30 and posting May 3. Use the letter date for citation and preserve metadata discrepancy without inferring an actual submission date.
sources.brief_exact_phrase: Reserve income flows from the issuer to the exchange, which may pass a portion to retail holders.
sources.page_context_paraphrase: Section I describes reserve-income routing. Section II then recommends extending the prohibition to upstream economic value regardless of its label, including coordination or issuer-derived funds, and expressly prohibits direct or indirect benefits. Section III would catch nominal extra conditions. Section IV argues that recycling into wholesale deposits does not preserve community-bank funding.
sources.verification_result: The descriptive routing passage gains prohibitory meaning from the explicit recommendations that immediately follow. Supports A/B/C prohibition and the funding rationale. It does not oppose the issuer earning reserve income for itself. No distinct policy on genuine activity rewards is inferred from the anti-evasion necessary-condition test. Count the joint letter once, not separately by signatory.
sources.review_scope: Complete four-page contribution, including footnotes and signatory list, rechecked.

sources.document_title: National Community Reinvestment Coalition — consultation response
sources.document_version: Cover dated June 9, 2026; six-page letter, with conclusion/signature on image-based page 6 and retained OCR supplement.
sources.pinpoint: pp 2–3, §1 and note 2; cover p 1; conclusion p 6
sources.brief_exact_phrase: Yield provisions and presumption do not go far enough to prevent deposit flight.
sources.page_context_paraphrase: The letter describes reserve interest routed through exchanges, then argues that the proposed restrictions are insufficient. It links deposit flight to lending costs and community investment, including loss of infrastructure in underserved areas. Its sentence about activity rewards being allowed describes the proposal; it is not a recommendation to permit them.
sources.verification_result: Supports stronger A/B/C restrictions, with D ambiguous and E no position retained. The overall ambiguous field follows the category mix and does not negate the explicit call for a stronger ban. The manuscript attributes funding/community-access concerns; its later discussion of tokenized-deposit runs should not be recoded as a remuneration-linked stability rationale.
sources.review_scope: All six pages of text, including retained OCR of page 6, rechecked. Operative remuneration section is pp 2–3.
